source.title: On Optimal Early Stopping: Over-informative versus Under-informative Parametrization
source.authors: Ruoqi Shen; Liyao (Mars) Gao; Yi-An Ma

record.tranche_reason: The paper reports test-error behavior over training epochs in deep networks and sample-size sweeps, using its own experiments and early-stopping analysis rather than reproducing the original study's full protocol.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports optimal stopping time versus model size and sample size. Those stopping-time trends are not test-error results, so they are not rows. The cited double-descent results from other work are not recorded as study results.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own epoch-wise test-error curves for MNIST, CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 networks, which bear on V2. It also derives and simulates risk at optimal early stopping as sample size varies in linear models, which bears on V6's claim that optimally tuned regularization removes the peak. Double descent is a secondary topic; the main focus is optimal stopping time.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors' main conclusion concerns optimal early stopping time, which behaves oppositely in over- and under-informative parametrizations. They show theoretically and in simulation that risk at optimal early stopping falls monotonically with sample size, mitigating sample-wise double descent. The statement that model-wise double descent can persist at optimal early stopping is cited from Nakkiran et al., not their own result.
record.recipe_differences: The paper analyzes early stopping in specified linear-regression models and runs nonlinear-network experiments; it does not reproduce the original double-descent protocol.
record.method_sensitivity: Results differ between over- and under-informative parametrizations and depend on whether risk is measured at optimal early stopping; experiments also vary datasets, architectures, model width, and sample size.

fits_no_version.finding: Optimal early stopping time decreases with model width and increases with sample size in the over-informative regime, and reverses in the under-informative regime (Figures 1, 2, 4-7, 13-15).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The optimal early-stopping time depends on whether model dimension exceeds the number of informative features.

record.problems: Most relevant curve results are presented as plots without numerical values. The sample-size plots do not locate the interpolation threshold, and the paper's monotonic sample-size results often concern risk at optimal early stopping rather than an unregularized curve.
record.rows_left_out: Optimal-stopping-time trends in Figures 1, 2, 4, 5(a), and Appendix E.1 Figures 6-7 were omitted because they measure stopping time rather than test error or risk. Figure 8's model-size-only trend for under-informative risk was omitted because the listed versions do not test that setting.

untested.parts: No unregularized model-size sweep of test error.
No unregularized sample-size sweep near the interpolation threshold; Figure 12's regime is unclear.
No capacity-risk curve across model classes past interpolation.
No effective-complexity measure predicting peak location.
Whether label noise drives the peak, multiple peaks, and model-wise peak removal under optimal early stopping in deep networks.

missing.what: Under-informative linear model: risk at optimal early stopping decreases with model size d (model-wise, regularized).
Test error versus epoch for CIFAR-100 ResNets of several widths with 20% noise, a further epoch-wise curve.

record.verdict_notes: The V3 rows were re-linked to V6 because they measure risk under optimally tuned early stopping, not the unregularized curve V3 describes. The deep-network double-descent evidence is figure-only, taken from captions. Neither original source is this study.

versions.untested_parts: No reported test-error sweep over model size that establishes the fall-rise-fall curve near the training-set interpolation point.
The reported epoch-wise results cover the named image datasets and tested networks, not all deep networks or training settings.
The sample-size results do not locate or test a neighborhood of the interpolation threshold; several results concern models stopped at their optimal early-stopping time.
The paper does not test a general capacity-risk curve across model classes past the interpolation point.
No single effective-complexity measure is tested as a predictor of peak location.
Label noise is used in experiments, but the paper does not test whether noise causes the peak, multiple peaks, or whether optimally tuned regularization removes it.
The paper does not re-count complexity using effective parameters or test whether that turns a second descent into an ordinary U-shape.

rows.subject: over-informative linear regression model
rows.operation_detail: varied sample size and evaluated expected risk at the approximated optimal early-stopping time
rows.measure: expected risk at optimal early stopping time
rows.value: the lower and upper risk bounds decrease monotonically as n increases
rows.note: This is a theoretical result for the paper's over-informative linear-regression setting.
rows.check: Wrongly linked to V3 as reversed. This is risk under optimal early stopping, a tuned regularizer. The authors say it 'can mitigate sample-wise double descent', which bears on V6's regularization clause, not on V3's unregularized claim. It is a theoretical bound, not an empirical measurement.

rows.check: This is risk at optimal early stopping in the under-informative setting, so it bears on V6's regularization clause, not V3. The bound holds only under the stated assumption that n and d are small relative to p, so it may not reach an interpolation regime.
